linkedin.text:
A destination brief is a strategy document — most companies just don't treat it that way.

The location you select for a leadership summit, a sales incentive trip, or a product launch shapes participant mindset before the first session begins. It signals investment. It signals intent.

Since 2010, with 130+ destinations, we've seen the same pattern: organizations that treat the destination as a strategic lever — not a logistics checkbox — consistently report stronger engagement and better post-event survey scores.

If you're planning a major event and haven't locked the destination yet, that decision deserves more than a shortlist on a spreadsheet.

Happy to share how we approach destination selection for specific objectives. DM me or drop your event type in the comments.

facebook.text:
The venue you choose tells your team something before a single word of your agenda is spoken.

We've produced events across 130+ destinations — and the ones that move the needle aren't always the most obvious choices. Sometimes it's a lesser-known coastal city. Sometimes it's a capital that surprises people who thought they'd seen it all.

The right destination doesn't just host your event. It does half the motivational work for you.
